interpretation.diagram_classification: cosmological / computistic diagram (annus: year, seasons, qualities of the elements)
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram is a schematic representation of the year (ANNVS, written at the centre) divided into the four seasons, each tied to a pair of qualities. Overlapping circles arranged around the centre carry the labels humidus, calidus, siccus and frigidus. The seasons are written between the circles: uer o ri ens (ver oriens, spring, east), eftas meridies (aestas meridies, summer, south), autumnus occidens (autumnus occidens, autumn, west) and hiemſ septentrio (hiems septentrio, winter, north). Spring is humid and warm, summer warm and dry, autumn dry and cold, and winter cold and humid. Each quality is shared by two neighbouring seasons, which is why each circle overlaps two seasonal zones. The result is a ring of eight overlapping lobes, each quality appearing twice. The diagram thus combines the cycle of the seasons, the four cardinal directions and the four qualities. These are the usual correspondences of the four elements and the four humours in the natural-philosophical and computistic tradition of the early medieval period.
interpretation.evidence: The title "AN NV s" at the centre is read as ANNVS. The qualities humidus, calidus (also spelled "caludus"), siccus ("ficcay", "ficcuf", with long s) and frigidus are all legible inside the circles. The seasonal terms are legible in fragments, such as "uer o ri ens", "eftas me ri dies", "autum nus oc ci dens" and "hiemſ sep ten tri o". The pairing of these terms follows the standard scheme of seasons, cardinal points and qualities, which is external knowledge. Some of the cardinal terms are partly illegible and have been completed on the basis of this scheme. Step 1 treated the seasonal words as free-standing text and read some of them hesitantly (for instance "ri" for "tri" and the last line of the autumn text). These are readings, not interpretations. Step 1 also gave the circles only as relations to the outer ring and to neighbouring circles, without the seasonal reading.

interpretation.diagram_classification: structural reading of the circles and their overlaps
interpretation.interpretation: The eight overlapping circles form a ring around the central word. Each circle represents one elemental quality, and its overlap with the next circle represents the season where two qualities meet. The colours of the bands (yellow, brown and green) mark the circles and their crossings. The outer yellow ring encloses the whole system and stands for the closed cycle of the year. No colour clearly corresponds to one quality, so the colours seem decorative or used for distinguishing the arcs. The circles are arranged so that opposite qualities (humid and dry, warm and cold) lie across the centre from each other.
interpretation.evidence: The outer ring contains the eight circles and the central title. Adjacent circles overlap at the places where the season names are written. The colours alternate between circles without a clear pattern, so the colour reading is uncertain. The pairing of opposites is inferred from the labels and their positions and is not stated in the diagram. Step 1 entry 14 treats two yellow arcs at the lower right as possibly separate circles or one large circle (low certainty), so the exact number of circles is uncertain. Step 1 also uses "connected_to" between circles that merely overlap, a loose use of the predicate.
